newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official says taxes obstacle in budget talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official says taxes obstacle in budget talks.

text.p: An admininistration official said on Thursday that tax cuts remain a sticking point in the talks between White House and congressional negotiators on balancing the U.S. federal budget by 2002.

"One of the issues still to be resolved is how to control the tax cuts in the outyears so that they don't balloon the budget deficit after 2002," said the official, who asked not to be named. "The president is very concerned about that."

Earlier, Republican Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and a White House spokesman both said they did not expect there to be any announcement on the budget on Thursday, with Lott saying that he was hopeful for an announcement on Friday.

Administration officials suggested that if President Bill Clinton were to make a budget announcement on Friday, he would likely do so around midday, after dedicating a memorial to Franklin Delano Roosevelt in the morning and before meeting Senate Democrats at an afternoon retreat in Baltimore, Maryland.
